title: Python & TD Craft
grandGoal: Get good enough at Python for a pipeline-TD role — building tools a whole team relies on — and to ship your own Blender extensions publicly.
note: Blender track targets 4.2 LTS and newer, where add-ons are Extensions with a blender_manifest.toml rather than the old bl_info dict. Tooling track uses the current standard stack: uv, Ruff, pytest, and a type checker.

nodes.title: Syntax & Control Flow
nodes.unlocks: You can write a small script and explain every line of it.
study: Variables, the built-in types, operators, f-strings
if / elif / else, for, while, break, continue, else-on-loop
Truthiness — what counts as falsy and the bugs that follow
Functions: parameters, defaults, *args / **kwargs, return, scope
The mutable-default-argument trap
Reading a traceback properly instead of skimming to the last line
nodes.challenge: Write a command-line tool that takes a folder and prints a summary: file count by extension, total size, largest file.
nodes.proof: The script, and it runs on a folder you didn't write it against.

nodes.title: Data Structures in Anger
nodes.unlocks: You reach for the right container without thinking about it.
study: list, dict, set, tuple — cost and behaviour of each, not just syntax
Comprehensions for list / dict / set, and when they stop being readable
Slicing, unpacking, star-unpacking, enumerate, zip
sorted() with key functions; itemgetter and lambda
collections: defaultdict, Counter, deque, namedtuple
Shallow vs. deep copy — the aliasing bug everyone hits once
nodes.challenge: Parse a messy CSV or log file into a clean nested structure and answer three questions about it that would be painful by hand.

nodes.title: Idiomatic Python
nodes.unlocks: Your code starts reading like Python instead of translated C.
study: Iterators and generators; yield, and why it saves memory
Context managers and the with statement; contextlib
Decorators — writing them, and functools.wraps
Exceptions: custom classes, try/except/else/finally, never bare except
Type hints: annotations, Optional, Union, generics, and what they buy
The standard library tour: pathlib, itertools, functools, dataclasses
nodes.challenge: Refactor an earlier script using a generator, a context manager and a decorator — each earning its place, not shoehorned in.
nodes.proof: Before and after, with a note on what each change bought.

nodes.title: Classes & Objects
nodes.unlocks: You can model a problem with your own types.
study: class, __init__, attributes, methods, and what self really is
Instance vs. class attributes — a classic source of shared-state bugs
Dunder methods: __str__, __repr__, __eq__, __len__
@property, @staticmethod, @classmethod
dataclasses — and why they replace most boilerplate classes
Composition over inheritance, with a concrete example of each
nodes.challenge: Build a small asset-manager library: an Asset type, a collection that holds them, JSON save/load, and a search.
nodes.proof: The module plus a script that uses it without touching internals.

nodes.title: Architecture & Patterns
nodes.unlocks: You can structure a tool so it survives other people changing it.
study: Separating core logic from the UI layer — the single most useful rule for TD work
Dependency injection in plain Python, without a framework
Patterns that actually come up: Strategy, Observer, Factory, Adapter
ABCs and Protocols for defining an interface
Module and package layout; __init__.py and public API surface
Configuration handling and avoiding hard-coded paths
nodes.challenge: Take a working tool and split it so the logic runs headless with no Blender import at all, with the UI as a thin shell over it.
nodes.proof: The logic layer under test with no bpy imported.

nodes.title: Git & Environments
nodes.unlocks: You can version work and reproduce an environment on another machine.
study: Git: commit, branch, merge, rebase, .gitignore, resolving conflicts
GitHub: repos, pull requests, issues, and a README worth reading
Virtual environments, and why never to install into system Python
uv for environments and dependency management, and committing uv.lock
pyproject.toml as the single place project config lives
Command line basics — pipeline work happens there
nodes.challenge: Publish one earlier script as a GitHub repo with a pyproject.toml, a locked environment and a README a stranger could follow.
nodes.proof: The repo URL, cloned fresh and run from the README alone.

nodes.title: Testing & Quality
nodes.unlocks: You can change code without fear because something else checks it.
study: pytest: test functions, assertions, fixtures, parametrize
What is worth testing — and what testing is a waste of time on
Mocking and monkeypatching, especially for code that touches the filesystem
Ruff for linting and formatting, configured in pyproject.toml
A type checker (mypy or pyright) in CI
GitHub Actions: run tests and lint on every push
Logging done properly — levels, handlers, never print() in a tool
nodes.challenge: Get one project to a green CI badge: tests, lint and type check all running on push.
nodes.proof: A passing Actions run on the repo.

nodes.title: Files, Paths & Formats
nodes.unlocks: You can move data between tools without hand-editing anything.
study: pathlib for every path operation — never string concatenation
Reading and writing text and binary safely, with encodings understood
JSON: load, dump, and custom encoders for your own types
CSV, and when a spreadsheet is the wrong answer
YAML/TOML for configuration; tomllib in the standard library
Atomic writes and backups — not corrupting a file on a failed run
nodes.challenge: Write a converter between two real formats you use, that survives malformed input without losing data.
nodes.proof: The converter plus a test with deliberately broken input.

nodes.title: APIs, Databases & Scraping
nodes.unlocks: You can pull data from somewhere else and make it useful.
study: HTTP basics: methods, status codes, headers, JSON payloads
requests / httpx: calling an API, handling errors, retries and timeouts
Authentication patterns and keeping secrets out of source control
SQLite with the sqlite3 module — enough SQL to be dangerous
Rate limiting, caching and being a polite client
Scheduling: cron or Task Scheduler for jobs that must just run
nodes.challenge: Build a tool that pulls from an API on a schedule, stores results in SQLite, and reports what changed since last time.
nodes.proof: The tool plus two runs showing a detected change.

nodes.title: bpy Fundamentals
nodes.unlocks: You can drive Blender from the console instead of clicking.
study: The four pillars: bpy.data, bpy.context, bpy.ops, bpy.types
bpy.data for direct data-block access — the reliable way to work
Why bpy.ops is context-dependent and fragile in scripts
The Python Console and Info editor for discovering calls
Creating, duplicating and deleting objects, meshes and materials in code
Collections, parenting and transforms via the API
Overriding context when an operator genuinely is the only option
nodes.challenge: Script a scene from nothing: geometry, materials, lights and a camera, then render it — without touching the UI once.
nodes.proof: The script and its render, run from a fresh Blender.

nodes.title: Mesh Data & bmesh
nodes.unlocks: You can edit geometry itself, not just objects.
study: Mesh data: vertices, edges, polygons, loops — and how loops tie it together
bmesh: opening from a mesh, editing, writing back
Selection, and building geometry procedurally in bmesh
Custom data layers: UVs, vertex colours, attributes
Foreach_get / foreach_set for bulk transfer at speed
Matrices and mathutils: Vector, Matrix, Quaternion, and world vs. local space
nodes.challenge: Write a mesh tool that does real work — a retopo helper, a UV checker, a geometry validator that reports problems.
nodes.proof: The tool run on a messy mesh, with its report.

nodes.title: Operators, Panels & Properties
nodes.unlocks: You can give a script a real interface inside Blender.
study: bpy.types.Operator: bl_idname, bl_label, poll(), execute(), invoke()
Registration and unregistration, and why the lifecycle matters
bpy.types.Panel and laying out UI with the layout API
Property types: StringProperty, EnumProperty, PointerProperty and friends
Where to store settings: Scene, Object, or AddonPreferences
Modal operators and handlers for anything long-running
undo_push and keeping the undo stack honest
nodes.challenge: Turn one of your scripts into a proper tool with a panel, exposed settings that persist in the .blend, and working undo.
nodes.proof: A screen recording: change settings, run, undo cleanly.

nodes.title: Ship an Extension
nodes.unlocks: Strangers can install your tool and it keeps working.
study: Extensions (Blender 4.2+): blender_manifest.toml replaces the old bl_info
Declaring permissions, and bundling wheels for Python dependencies
Building and validating locally with blender --command extension build
Publishing to extensions.blender.org, and the review expectations
Versioning, changelogs, and not breaking users on update
Supporting multiple Blender versions without branching the code
Handling user bug reports and writing docs people actually read
nodes.challenge: Publish one extension that solves a real problem you personally hit, with docs and a version history.
nodes.proof: The listing URL, or the built .zip installing cleanly from scratch.

nodes.title: Batch & Headless
nodes.unlocks: You can make Blender do work with nobody watching.
study: blender --background --python for headless jobs
Passing arguments to a script past the -- separator
Batch rendering, batch import/export, and processing whole folders
Render layers and command-line frame ranges for splitting jobs
Failing loudly: exit codes and logs a scheduler can act on
Wrapping it all in a CLI with argparse
nodes.challenge: Build a batch tool that processes an entire folder of .blend files unattended and writes a report of what it did.
nodes.proof: A log from a run over at least five files, including one that failed on purpose.

nodes.title: Pipeline Tooling
nodes.unlocks: You can build the thing a team depends on daily.
study: Asset libraries and the Asset Browser API
Linking vs. appending, library overrides, and why productions link
Naming conventions and folder structures enforced by tooling, not by hope
Publish/version systems: what a 'publish' actually guarantees
USD and Alembic interchange between applications
Validation tools that catch problems before they reach the renderer
Rolling out a tool to other people, and supporting it afterwards
nodes.challenge: Build a small end-to-end pipeline: ingest, validate, publish, and pull back into a scene — with rules enforced by code.
nodes.proof: A walkthrough of an asset going the whole way through.

nodes.title: Performance & Scale
nodes.unlocks: Your tools stay usable on production-sized data.
study: Profiling first: cProfile and timeit, before optimising anything
NumPy for bulk numeric work, and foreach_get into arrays
Avoiding per-element Python loops over mesh data
Threads vs. processes in Python, and where the GIL actually bites
Keeping the UI responsive: modal operators and timers
Memory: generators, chunking, and not loading a scene twice
Caching results that are expensive and stable
nodes.challenge: Take a tool that crawls on a heavy scene and make it at least 10x faster, with profiler output proving where the time went.
